docs.title: Home
docs.text:
AsMysql Asynchronous MySQL Client Library
  • • asmysql is an asynchronous MySQL client library based on aiomysql, designed for Python asynchronous programming.
  • • The v2 version has completely refactored the architecture, providing a clearer and more flexible API design, supporting type hints, connection pool management, error handling, and other enterprise-level features.
🚀 Simple & Easy

Intuitive API design with low learning curve, quick to get started

⚡ High Performance

Asynchronous operations based on connection pool, supporting high concurrency

🔧 Type Safe

Complete type hint support for better development experience

💾 Memory Friendly

Supports streaming queries, handling large datasets without memory consumption

🔌 Flexible Extension

Separated engine and business logic for better architecture design

🪶 Ultra Lightweight

Minimal code size, no redundant dependencies, simple deployment

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install asmysql

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
import asyncio
from asmysql import Engine

async def main():
    # Create engine
    engine = Engine(
        host='localhost',
        port=3306,
        user='root',
        password='password',
    )

    # Connect to database
    await engine.connect()

    # Execute query
    async with engine.execute("SELECT user, host FROM mysql.user") as result:
        async for item in result.iterate():
            print(item)

    # Close connection
    await engine.disconnect()

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: 1. Separated Architecture
docs.text:
• Engine class: Independent MySQL connection engine, can be used standalone
  • AsMysql class: Business logic development base class, ready to use by inheritance
  • Result class: Result processing class, supporting multiple data retrieval methods

docs.title: 2. Connection Management
docs.text:
• Automatic MySQL connection pool management
  • Support for connection pool configuration (min/max connections)
  • Automatic reconnection mechanism
  • Connection status monitoring
  • Connection init SET SQL (init_sql): Automatically execute preset SQL on each new TCP connection's first use (ideal for MySQL session variables; re-executed after connection rebuilds)

docs.title: 3. Flexible Query Methods
docs.text:
• Support for regular queries and streaming queries
  • Support for single and batch execution
  • Reliable auto-commit: persisted on success, rolled back on failure (server autocommit + transaction-state fallback)

docs.title: 4. Multiple Result Types
docs.text:
• tuple: Default tuple type
  • dict: Dictionary type
  • Custom models: Support for Pydantic and other model classes

docs.title: 5. Data Retrieval Methods
docs.text:
• fetch_one(): Get a single record
  • fetch_many(): Get multiple records
  • fetch_all(): Get all records
  • iterate(): Async iterator, get records row by row
  • Direct iteration: async for item in result

docs.title: 6. Error Handling
docs.text:
• Global automatic capture of MysqlError
  • Error code and error message access
  • Elegant error handling mechanism

docs.title: 7. Context Management
docs.text:
• Support for async with syntax
  • Automatic resource cleanup
  • Support for async iterator protocol

docs.title: 8. URL Connection String

  • Format: mysql://user:password@host:port/?charset=utf8mb4

docs.text: asmysql provides development support for AI coding assistants (Claude Code / Cursor / Qoder / Codex, etc.): a user-level development skill (usage quickref + pitfall guide + doc map) and LLM-friendly plain-text documentation entries, so AI finds correct usage on first contact with asmysql and avoids high-frequency pitfalls.

docs.title: Option 1: One-Command Skill Install (Recommended)
docs.text:
Run at your project root (--target is required; project-level preferred):

python -m asmysql skill install --target claude

--target values:

Value Scope Behavior claude / cursor Project Canonical ./.agents/skills/asmysql-dev/ + per-skill symlink in the tool directory agents Project Install the canonical only, no symlinks user:claude / user:cursor / user:agents User Same layout, rooted at ~/ all / user:all Project / User Canonical install + symlinks only into existing tool directories (missing ones never created) Any path Custom Expands ~; under a project with existing .agents/skills/ reuses its canonical + symlink, otherwise the entity lands directly in the custom directory

Comma-separated multi-targets are supported (e.g. --target claude,user:cursor). The install model is "single canonical + per-skill symlinks": one entity per scope (with a version stamp), shared by tool-directory symlinks; symlink failure falls back to an entity copy. Existing targets are skipped by default; after upgrading asmysql, refresh with --force:

python -m asmysql skill install --target claude --force

docs.text:

docs.text:
def __init__(
    self,
    url: str = None,
    *,
    host: str = None,
    port: int = None,
    user: str = None,
    password: str = None,
    charset: str = None,
    min_pool_size: int = None,
    max_pool_size: int = None,
    pool_recycle: float = None,
    connect_timeout: int = None,
    echo_sql_log: bool = None,
    init_sql: str = None,
    disconnect_timeout: float = None,
) -> None

Parameter Description:

  • url (str, optional): MySQL connection URL, format: mysql://user:password@host:port/?charset=utf8mb4
  • host (str, optional): MySQL server address
  • port (int, optional): MySQL server port
  • user (str, optional): Username
  • password (str, optional): Password
  • charset (str, optional): Character set
  • min_pool_size (int, optional): Minimum connection pool size
  • max_pool_size (int, optional): Maximum connection pool size
  • pool_recycle (float, optional): Idle connection recycle time (seconds)
  • connect_timeout (int, optional): Connection timeout (seconds)
  • echo_sql_log (bool, optional): Whether to print SQL logs
  • init_sql (str, optional): SET SQL to auto-execute on connection init, executed once per new TCP connection on first use
  • disconnect_timeout (float, optional): disconnect wait timeout (seconds); None (default) waits forever, a finite value forces terminate on timeout; none in URL means None

Examples:

# Using URL
engine = Engine(url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/?charset=utf8mb4")

# Using keyword arguments
engine = Engine(host="127.0.0.1", port=3306, user="root", password="pass", charset="utf8mb4")

docs.title: connect()
docs.text:
Connect to MySQL, establish TCP connection, initialize connection pool. The pool is fixed at autocommit=True (built-in library behavior, no configuration parameter); if a backend rejects the handshake, the library internally falls back to the server default and emits a warning. If init_sql is configured, each new TCP connection will automatically execute the init SQL on first use. Since v2.4.0, reuse across event loops is supported: after disconnecting in the original loop, you can connect again in a new loop (the internal lock is rebuilt per loop); connecting in a new loop while the pool is still alive raises ConnectionError.

async def connect(self) -> Engine

Return Value: Returns self, supports chaining

Example:

await engine.connect()

docs.title: disconnect()
docs.text:
Wait for all connections to be released and properly close MySQL connection. By default (disconnect_timeout=None) waits forever; with a finite timeout configured, emits a ResourceWarning on timeout and forcibly terminates all in-use connections; on cancellation also terminates and re-raises.

async def disconnect(self) -> None

Example:

await engine.disconnect()

docs.title: terminate()
docs.text:
Synchronously force-clean the connection pool (idempotent, since v2.5.0). Does not wait for connections to return: immediately closes all in-use connections and severs in-flight queries, then cleans up idle connections best-effort; suitable for atexit and synchronous shutdown hooks. Contrast with disconnect(): terminate = synchronous and forceful, disconnect = async graceful wait.

def terminate(self) -> None

After the call, is_connected is False and execute() raises ConnectionError; you can connect() again to reuse the Engine. A no-op when called before connect; explicit calls emit no warning.

Example:

import atexit

atexit.register(engine.terminate)  # synchronous hook, no event loop required

docs.title: release_connections()
docs.text:
Release all idle connections in the connection pool.

async def release_connections(self) -> None

Example:

await engine.release_connections()

docs.title: execute()
docs.text:
Execute SQL statement and return Result object.

def execute(
    self,
    query: str,
    values: Union[Sequence, dict] = None,
    *,
    stream: bool = None,
    result_class: type[T] = None,
) -> Union[AsyncContextManager[Result[T]], AsyncGenerator[T, None]]

Parameter Description:

  • query (str): SQL statement
  • values (Union[Sequence, dict], optional): Parameters, can be tuple or dict
  • stream (bool, optional): Whether to stream results, defaults to self.stream
  • result_class (type, optional): Result type, defaults to tuple

Return Value: Returns Result object, supports the following usages:

  1. async with engine.execute(...) as result:
  2. async for item in engine.execute(...):

Examples:

# Method 1: context manager
async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s", (1,)) as result:
    data = await result.fetch_one()

# Method 2: context manager + fetch_all
async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users") as result:
    data = await result.fetch_all()

# Method 3: direct iteration
async for row in engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users"):
    print(row)

docs.title: execute_many()
docs.text:
Batch execute SQL statements and return Result object. With an empty parameter list ([]), no connection is acquired and no SQL is executed; a UserWarning is emitted and row_count=0.

def execute_many(
    self,
    query: str,
    values: Sequence[Union[Sequence, dict]],
    *,
    stream: bool = None,
    result_class: type[T] = None,
) -> Union[AsyncContextManager[Result[T]], AsyncGenerator[T, None]]

Parameter Description:

  • query (str): SQL statement
  • values (Sequence[Union[Sequence, dict]]): Parameter list, each element can be tuple or dict
  • stream (bool, optional): Whether to stream results
  • result_class (type, optional): Result type

Return Value: Returns Result object

Example:

data = [("张三", "zhangsan@example.com"), ("李四", "lisi@example.com")]
async with engine.execute_many("INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (%s, %s)", data) as result:
    print(f"Inserted {result.row_count} records")

docs.title: del()
docs.text: GC safety net (since v2.5.0): if the Engine is reclaimed without being disconnect()ed, emits a ResourceWarning and calls terminate() for synchronous cleanup. Silent after disconnect()/terminate() or when never connected; never awaits and never resurrects references. Production code should still explicitly await engine.disconnect().

docs.title: AsMysql Class
docs.text: AsMysql is the base class for business logic development, used to encapsulate business methods.

docs.title: Class Definition
docs.text:
class AsMysql:
    """Class for writing MySQL business logic"""

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
def __init__(self, engine: Engine) -> None

Parameter Description:

  • engine (Engine): Engine instance

Example:

engine = Engine(url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/")
await engine.connect()


class UserService(AsMysql):
    pass


service = UserService(engine)

docs.title: Constructive Singleton
docs.text:
AsMysql implements a process-wide constructive singleton through __new__: instances are reused with (subclass, engine object) as the key.

def __new__(cls, engine: Engine) -> AsMysql
  • Same subclass + same engine object: returns the same instance; after a hit, __init__ runs again but only reassigns the same engine
  • Different engine objects: each keeps its own instance
  • Different subclasses + same engine object: independent and isolated
  • The instance table is a strong-reference cache and must be unregistered with release()

Example:

class UserService(AsMysql):
    pass


assert UserService(engine) is UserService(engine)

docs.title: Class Method release
docs.text:
Unregisters instance table entries (only releases strong references, does not call disconnect).

@classmethod
def release(cls, engine: Engine | None = None) -> int

Parameter Description:

  • engine (Engine, optional): when given, removes this engine's entries across all subclasses; when omitted, clears the whole table

Return Value: number of removed entries (int)

Example:

removed = UserService.release(engine)  # Remove entries for this engine
removed = UserService.release()  # Clear the whole table (lifespan shutdown)

Lifecycle and GC Semantics:

  • The instance table holds strong references to instances, so __del__ never triggers and instances are never unregistered by garbage collection
  • Deterministic cleanup uses release(); stale entries of disconnected engines (is_connected is False) are lazily removed on the next construction miss
  • release() does not call disconnect(); the connection pool is still closed by engine.disconnect()
  • Recommended shutdown order: await engine.disconnect() → release(engine) (order can be swapped)

docs.text:

@property
def client(self) -> Engine

Return Value: Engine instance

Example:

class UserService(AsMysql):
    async def get_users(self):

docs.title: fetch_one()
docs.text:
Get a single record.

async def fetch_one(self) -> Optional[T]

Return Value: Returns a single record, returns None if no data

Usage Constraint: must be used inside an async with / async for context, or paired with an explicit close(); bare execution + fetch without close is not recommended (triggers the GC discard safety net, see __del__()).

Example:

async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s", (1,)) as result:
    user = await result.fetch_one()
    if user:
        print(user)

docs.title: fetch_many()
docs.text:
Get multiple records.

async def fetch_many(self, size: int = None) -> list[T]

Parameter Description:

  • size (int, optional): Number of records to fetch, defaults to all available records

Return Value: Returns list of records

Usage Constraint: must be used inside an async with / async for context, or paired with an explicit close(); bare execution + fetch without close is not recommended (triggers the GC discard safety net, see __del__()).

Example:

async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users") as result:
    users = await result.fetch_many(10)  # Get 10 records

docs.title: fetch_all()
docs.text:
Get all records.

async def fetch_all(self) -> list[T]

Return Value: Returns list of all records

Note: This method will automatically close cursor connection

Example:

docs.title: iterate()
docs.text:
Async generator, iterate through all records.

async def iterate(self) -> AsyncGenerator[T, None]

Return Value: Async generator, returns records row by row

Note: This method will automatically close cursor connection

Example:

async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users") as result:
    async for user in result.iterate():
        print(user)

docs.title: close()
docs.text:
Close cursor and release connection. Safe to call repeatedly; after close, result.pool is cleared to None (since v2.5.0, caching closed Results no longer pins the Pool and the event loop). Executing an unexecuted Result after close raises RuntimeError.

async def close(self) -> None

Example:

async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users") as result:
    data = await result.fetch_one()
    # ... other operations
# Automatically closed on exiting async with

docs.title: error
docs.text:
Error exception object.

@property
def error(self) -> Optional[MySQLError]

Return Value: MySQLError exception object, returns None if no error

Since v2.4.0, the exception's __traceback__ is None (frame chain severed to prevent memory retention); use error_no / error_msg for troubleshooting.

Example:

async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM invalid_table") as result:
    if result.error:
        print(f"Error: {result.error}")

docs.text:

@property
def error_no(self) -> int

Return Value: Error code (integer), returns 0 if no error

Example:

@property
def error_msg(self) -> str

docs.text:
Number of affected rows.

@property

Return Value: - Number of affected rows (integer) - Returns None if error occurs - Returns None if using streaming query (stream=True)

Example:

docs.text:

@property

Return Value: - ID of the most recently inserted record (integer) - Returns None if no data inserted or error occurs

@property

Example:

docs.title: await()
docs.text:
Not implemented: Result does not support await result syntax (raises TypeError). This is a deliberate design decision to avoid leaks becoming the default usage.

Standard forms:

async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users") as result:
    data = await result.fetch_all()

async for row in engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users"):
    print(row)

docs.title: call()
docs.text:
Internal execution entry: called automatically by __aenter__ / __aiter__ / __anext__ to acquire a connection and execute the SQL (idempotent, executes only once).

async def __call__(self) -> Result[T]

Standalone use not recommended: after bare execution (await result()), the connection must be released via async with or an explicit close(); otherwise the connection is discarded (not reused) at GC with a ResourceWarning (since v2.6.0).

Example (standard form):

result = engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users")
async with result:
    data = await result.fetch_all()

docs.title: del()
docs.text: GC safety net (since v2.6.0): if an executed Result is reclaimed without being properly closed, synchronously discards the connection (closes the transport without sending COM_QUIT) and completes pool bookkeeping via pool.release(), emitting a ResourceWarning. The connection is not returned to the pool for reuse; uncommitted transactions are rolled back by the server and already auto-committed data is unaffected; disconnect() no longer hangs forever because of this. Silent when already closed or never executed; never awaits and never resurrects references. Production code must use async with / async for / close(); the safety net is only a fallback.

docs.title: 1. For Simple MySQL Connection Scenarios, Use Context Management
✅ Recommended: Use Context Manager
docs.text:

    # Execute SQL statement using context manager

    # Automatically disconnect MySQL connection on exit

docs.title: ❌ Not Recommended: Forget to Disconnect
docs.text:
await engine.connect()
async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users") as result:
    pass
# Forgot await engine.disconnect()

docs.title: 2. About Connection Resource Management
docs.text: Result objects returned by execute() / execute_many() must be used via async with or async for to ensure proper connection release:

docs.title: ✅ Recommended: Use Context Manager (Automatic Connection Management)
docs.text:
When using async with, the connection will be automatically closed when exiting the context:

async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users") as result:
    data = await result.fetch_one()
    # Automatically close connection on exit

docs.title: ✅ Recommended: Use async for (Automatic Connection Management)
docs.text:
When using async for, the connection will be automatically closed after iteration completes:

async for item in engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users"):
    print(item)
    # Automatically close connection after iteration completes

docs.title: ⚠️ Note: Must Use async with or async for
docs.text:
execute() returns a Result object (not a coroutine) and cannot be awaited. It must be used via async with or async for:

# ✅ Correct: Use async with
async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users") as result:
    data = await result.fetch_one()

# ✅ Correct: Use async for
async for item in engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users"):
    print(item)

# ❌ Wrong: Cannot await (execute is not a coroutine)
# result = await engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users")

# ❌ Not recommended: bare execution + fetch without close
# r = engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users")
# await r()
# row = await r.fetch_one()
# # Forgot await r.close() → connection discarded (not reused) at GC with ResourceWarning

Important Notes: - Result objects must be used via async with or async for (or paired with an explicit close()); these are the only recommended standard forms - Since v2.6.0, an improperly closed Result that is garbage-collected has its connection synchronously discarded with pool bookkeeping completed (no longer leaking permanently or hanging disconnect()), but this is only a fallback for misuse: the connection is not reused, uncommitted transactions are rolled back, and a ResourceWarning is emitted - When using context manager or async for, connections are automatically managed by the framework

docs.title: ✅ Recommended: Check Errors
docs.text:
async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users") as result:
    if result.error:
        logger.error(f"Query failed: {result.error_msg}")
        return []
    return await result.fetch_all()

docs.title: ❌ Not Recommended: Ignore Errors
docs.text:
async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users") as result:
    data = await result.fetch_all()  # If error occurs, data may be empty list

docs.title: ✅ Recommended: Use Streaming Query
docs.text:
async for row in engine.execute("SELECT * FROM large_table", stream=True):
    process(row)

docs.title: ❌ Not Recommended: Load All Data at Once
docs.text:
async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM large_table") as result:
    all_data = await result.fetch_all()  # May cause memory overflow

docs.title: ✅ Recommended: Use Parameterized Queries to Prevent SQL Injection
docs.text:
async with engine.execute(
    "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = %s",
    (user_name,)
) as result:
    users = await result.fetch_all()

docs.title: ❌ Not Recommended: String Concatenation
docs.text:
async with engine.execute(
    f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '{user_name}'"
) as result:
    users = await result.fetch_all()

docs.title: ✅ Recommended: Configure Connection Pool Based on Application Load
docs.text:
engine = Engine(
    url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/",
    min_pool_size=5,   # Maintain minimum connections
    max_pool_size=50,  # Set maximum based on concurrency
    pool_recycle=3600  # Recycle idle connections after 1 hour
)

docs.title: ❌ Not Recommended: Use Default Values (May Not Be Suitable for Production)
docs.text: engine = Engine(url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/")

docs.title: Inherit AsMysql Class
docs.text:
The AsMysql class provides a base class for business logic development, making it convenient to organize code through inheritance:

from asmysql import Engine, AsMysql

class UserService(AsMysql):
    async def get_user_by_id(self, user_id: int):
        async with self.client.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s",
            (user_id,),
            result_class=dict
        ) as result:
            if result.error:
                return None
            return await result.fetch_one()

    async def create_user(self, name: str, email: str):
        async with self.client.execute(
            "INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (%s, %s)",
            (name, email)
        ) as result:
            if result.error:
                raise Exception(f"Failed to create user: {result.error_msg}")
            return result.last_rowid

    async def list_users(self):
        async with self.client.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM users",
            result_class=dict
        ) as result:
            if result.error:
                return []
            return await result.fetch_all()

docs.text:
# Create engine
engine = Engine(url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/")
await engine.connect()

# Create business logic instance
user_service = UserService(engine)

# Use business methods

users = await user_service.list_users()
new_user_id = await user_service.create_user("张三", "zhangsan@example.com")

docs.title: Instance Reuse (Constructive Singleton)
docs.text:
The AsMysql base class provides a built-in process-wide constructive singleton: instances are reused with (subclass, engine object) as the key, so business subclasses need no singleton code.

  • Same subclass + same engine object: always reuse the same instance
  • Different engine objects: each keeps its own instance
  • Different subclasses + same engine object: isolated from each other
engine = Engine(url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/")
await engine.connect()

class OrderService(AsMysql):
    pass

assert UserService(engine) is UserService(engine)       # same instance
assert UserService(engine) is not OrderService(engine)  # isolated per subclass

docs.title: Releasing Instances
docs.text:
The instance table holds strong references to engines. After an engine is disconnected, its stale entries are automatically removed on the next instance creation; you can also unregister explicitly when the application shuts down or a task round finishes:

# Remove this engine's entries across all subclasses, returns the removed count
removed = UserService.release(engine)

# Clear the whole table (e.g., Web service lifespan shutdown), returns the removed count
removed = UserService.release()

Note: release() only releases the instance table's strong references to engines; it does not disconnect them. The connection pool is still closed by whoever owns the engine via engine.disconnect().

docs.title: Lifecycle and GC Semantics
docs.text:
The instance table holds strong references to instances keyed by (subclass, engine object), so reference counts never drop to zero:

  • AsMysql has no __del__ cleanup path; instances are never unregistered by garbage collection;
  • Lazy removal only runs when a new instance misses the table, and only removes engine entries whose is_connected is False;
  • In a long-running process that repeatedly creates and disconnects engines without constructing new instances afterwards, stale entries remain until an explicit release() or process exit.

Recommended shutdown order:

# Web lifespan shutdown / end of each CLI round
await engine.disconnect()      # close the connection pool first
UserService.release(engine)    # then unregister this engine's instance entries

release() does not depend on engine connection state, so the two steps can be swapped; it only releases the table's strong references and never calls disconnect() for you.

docs.title: Disconnect Wait Policy (disconnect_timeout)
docs.text:
disconnect() must wait for all connections to return (unclosed Result objects still hold connections):

  • None (default): waits forever, consistent with legacy behavior; make sure all Result objects are closed;
  • Finite value (e.g. 0.5): after the graceful wait times out, emits a ResourceWarning and forcibly terminates all in-use connections, guaranteed to converge; in-flight queries receive error_no=2013;
  • <= 0: no wait, terminate immediately.
# When convergence guarantees are needed, configure explicitly based on the longest business execution time
engine = Engine(url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/", disconnect_timeout=30)

docs.title: Synchronous Forced Cleanup: terminate()
docs.text:
terminate() is a synchronous forced cleanup method (since v2.5.0), complementary to the async graceful disconnect():

Method Semantics Typical scenarios await disconnect() Gracefully waits for all connections to return (see disconnect_timeout) Normal shutdown inside an event loop terminate() Synchronous and forceful: no waiting for returns, immediately closes all in-use connections and severs in-flight queries atexit, synchronous shutdown hooks, fallback cleanup 
import atexit

engine = Engine(url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/")
atexit.register(engine.terminate)  # synchronous hook, no event loop required

Behavior notes:

  • Idempotent; a no-op when called before connect; explicit calls emit no warning;
  • After the call, is_connected is False and execute() raises ConnectionError; you can connect() again to reuse the Engine;
  • In-use connections are closed immediately (aiomysql Pool.terminate()); a late result.close() is safe; in-flight queries receive a connection-lost error;
  • Idle connections are cleaned up best-effort: this relies on the aiomysql private attribute _free and defensively degrades to terminate-only when it is missing or changes shape; when the event loop is already closed, per-connection close exceptions are isolated and never propagate.

__del__ safety net: if an Engine is garbage-collected without being disconnect()ed, it automatically emits a ResourceWarning and calls terminate() for synchronous cleanup, instead of relying on Connection.__del__ (warning noise, delayed cyclic GC, RuntimeError when the loop is already closed). GC is silent after disconnect()/terminate() or when never connected. Production code should still explicitly await engine.disconnect(); the safety net is only a fallback.

docs.title: Reuse Across Event Loops
docs.text:
An Engine can be reused across multiple event loops (e.g. multiple asyncio.run() calls), but must follow the "disconnect in the original loop → connect in the new loop" pattern:

engine = Engine(url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/")


async def job():
    await engine.connect()
    async with engine.execute("SELECT 1") as result:
        print(await result.fetch_one())
    await engine.disconnect()


asyncio.run(job())  # Event loop 1
asyncio.run(job())  # Event loop 2: the internal lock is rebuilt and the pool is recreated

Constraints:

  • An aiomysql pool is bound to its event loop at creation time; a live pool cannot be shared across loops: with the pool still connected, calling connect(), accessing engine.pool, or calling execute() in a new loop raises a ConnectionError with a clear message;
  • An abandoned Engine whose loop has closed without disconnecting is not guaranteed to be cleanable in a new loop; always disconnect within the original loop;
  • Concurrent connect() calls within the same loop are still serialized by the internal lock; behavior is unchanged.

docs.title: Connection Init SQL (init_sql)
docs.text: The init_sql parameter automatically executes preset SQL on each new TCP connection's first use. Ideal for setting session-level variables, such as MySQL session variables (time_zone, sql_mode, and other settings without query-level syntax). For ClickHouse async inserts, the query-level SETTINGS clause is recommended instead (see below).

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
• init_sql execution is implemented in Result.__call__(), not at connect() stage
  • Uses weakref.WeakKeyDictionary with Pool as key and a WeakSet tracking initialized connections by object identity (no id-based tracking, avoiding address reuse)
  • Executes on an independent buffered cursor that is closed immediately, without affecting streaming business cursors
  • Executes init_sql on first SQL execution of a new connection; skips on subsequent reuses
  • When a connection is recycled via pool_recycle, the new connection re-executes init_sql
  • If init_sql fails: the main SQL is not executed, the error is written to result.error, and the connection is discarded instead of reused
  • Modifying autocommit in init_sql is not recommended; if required, the client falls back to commit/rollback based on server transaction state — functionally correct, but the semantics are your responsibility

docs.title: ClickHouse Async Insert Configuration
docs.text:
Recommended: query-level SETTINGS clause (zero extra round-trips, no session state, execute_many compatible):

from asmysql import Engine

engine = Engine(host="192.168.62.195", port=9004, user="default", password="")
await engine.connect()

# wait_for_async_insert=1: waits for the async flush to complete, failures are visible; do not use 0 (fire-and-forget cannot guarantee persistence)
async with engine.execute(
    "INSERT INTO audit_log SETTINGS async_insert=1, wait_for_async_insert=1 VALUES (%s, %s)",
    ("event", "payload"),
) as result:
    pass

Optional alternative: init_sql session-level settings (executed once per new connection):

from asmysql import Engine

engine = Engine(
    host="192.168.62.195",
    port=9004,
    user="default",
    password="",
    init_sql="SET async_insert = 1, wait_for_async_insert = 1",
)
await engine.connect()

# All subsequent execute() calls automatically run SET on new connections
async with engine.execute("INSERT INTO audit_log ...") as result:
    pass

docs.title: ClickHouse Async Inserts (Query-Level SETTINGS)
docs.text:
The query-level SETTINGS clause on INSERT statements is recommended: zero extra round-trips, no session state, execute_many compatible. wait_for_async_insert=1 waits for the async flush to complete so failures are visible; do not use 0 (fire-and-forget cannot guarantee persistence).

import asyncio
from asmysql import Engine

async def main():
    engine = Engine(
        host="192.168.62.195",
        port=9004,
        user="default",
        password="",
    )
    await engine.connect()

    # Query-level SETTINGS: async insert with flush completion waited
    async with engine.execute(
        "INSERT INTO audit_log SETTINGS async_insert=1, wait_for_async_insert=1 "
        "(ts, msg) VALUES (%s, %s)",
        ("2025-01-01", "hello"),
    ) as result:
        if result.error:
            print(f"Insert failed: {result.error_msg}")

    await engine.disconnect()

asyncio.run(main())

        init_sql="SET async_insert = 1, wait_for_async_insert = 1",

    async with engine.execute("INSERT INTO audit_log (ts, msg) VALUES (%s, %s)", ("2025-01-01", "hello")) as result:
        if result.error:
            print(f"Insert failed: {result.error_msg}")

docs.title: Auto-Commit Mechanism
docs.text:
Since v2.3.0, a "server-side auto-commit + transaction-state fallback" mechanism is used: the pool is fixed at autocommit=True, writes are persisted on success, failed statements are rolled back automatically, and reads/writes are no longer distinguished by SQL keywords.

import asyncio
from asmysql import Engine

async def main():
    engine = Engine(url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/")
    await engine.connect()

    # Write operations are auto-committed by the server, no manual control needed
    async with engine.execute(
        "INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (%s, %s)",
        ("张三", "zhangsan@example.com")
    ) as result:
        if result.error:
            print(f"Insert failed: {result.error_msg}")
        else:
            print(f"Insert successful, ID: {result.last_rowid}")

    # Read operations have no open transaction, the client does not commit twice
    async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users") as result:
        data = await result.fetch_all()
        print(f"Queried {len(data)} records")

    await engine.disconnect()

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Commit Timing in Stream Mode
docs.text:
stream=True + writes without result sets are committed immediately after execution; for streaming statements with result sets, the transaction (if any) is deferred until the cursor closes to avoid breaking the streaming protocol.

from asmysql import Engine

async def main():
    engine = Engine(url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/")
    await engine.connect()

    # Streaming reads: the transaction (if any) is committed when the cursor closes after reading
    async with engine.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM large_table",
        stream=True
    ) as result:
        async for row in result:
            process(row)

    await engine.disconnect()

asyncio.run(main())

import asyncio
from typing import Optional, List
from pydantic import BaseModel
from asmysql import Engine, AsMysql

class User(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    email: str
    age: int = 0

class UserService(AsMysql):
    """User service class"""

    async def get_user_by_id(self, user_id: int) -> Optional[User]:
        """Get user by ID"""
        async with self.client.execute(
            "SELECT id, name, email, age FROM users WHERE id = %s",
            (user_id,),
            result_class=User
        ) as result:
            if result.error:
                return None
            return await result.fetch_one()

    async def get_user_by_email(self, email: str) -> Optional[User]:
        """Get user by email"""
        async with self.client.execute(
            "SELECT id, name, email, age FROM users WHERE email = %s",
            (email,),
            result_class=User
        ) as result:
            if result.error:
                return None
            return await result.fetch_one()

    async def list_users(self, limit: int = 100) -> List[User]:
        """Get user list"""
        async with self.client.execute(
            "SELECT id, name, email, age FROM users LIMIT %s",
            (limit,),
            result_class=User
        ) as result:
            if result.error:
                return []
            return await result.fetch_all()

    async def create_user(self, name: str, email: str, age: int = 0) -> Optional[int]:
        """Create user"""
        async with self.client.execute(
            "INSERT INTO users (name, email, age) VALUES (%s, %s, %s)",
            (name, email, age)
        ) as result:
            if result.error:
                return None
            return result.last_rowid

    async def update_user(self, user_id: int, name: str = None, email: str = None, age: int = None) -> bool:
        """Update user"""
        updates = []
        values = []

        if name is not None:
            updates.append("name = %s")
            values.append(name)
        if email is not None:
            updates.append("email = %s")
            values.append(email)
        if age is not None:
            updates.append("age = %s")
            values.append(age)

        if not updates:
            return False

        values.append(user_id)
        query = f"UPDATE users SET {', '.join(updates)} WHERE id = %s"

        async with self.client.execute(query, tuple(values)) as result:
            return result.error is None

    async def delete_user(self, user_id: int) -> bool:
        """Delete user"""
        async with self.client.execute(
            "DELETE FROM users WHERE id = %s",
            (user_id,)
        ) as result:
            return result.error is None

async def main():
    engine = Engine(url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/")
    await engine.connect()

    user_service = UserService(engine)

    # Create user
    user_id = await user_service.create_user("张三", "zhangsan@example.com", 25)
    print(f"Created user, ID: {user_id}")

    # Get user
    user = await user_service.get_user_by_id(user_id)
    if user:
        print(f"User: {user.name}, Email: {user.email}, Age: {user.age}")

    # Update user
    success = await user_service.update_user(user_id, age=26)
    print(f"Update user: {success}")

    # Get user list
    users = await user_service.list_users(10)
    print(f"User list, total {len(users)} records")

    await engine.disconnect()

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel
from asmysql import Engine, AsMysql
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

# Global engine
engine = Engine(url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/")

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    # Connect on startup
    await engine.connect()
    yield
    # Disconnect on shutdown
    await engine.disconnect()

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)

# Data models
class UserCreate(BaseModel):
    name: str
    email: str
    age: int = 0

class UserResponse(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    email: str
    age: int

# Service class
class UserService(AsMysql):
    async def create_user(self, user_data: UserCreate) -> int:
        async with self.client.execute(
            "INSERT INTO users (name, email, age) VALUES (%s, %s, %s)",
            (user_data.name, user_data.email, user_data.age)
        ) as result:
            if result.error:
                raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=result.error_msg)
            return result.last_rowid

    async def get_user(self, user_id: int) -> UserResponse:
        async with self.client.execute(
            "SELECT id, name, email, age FROM users WHERE id = %s",
            (user_id,),
            result_class=UserResponse
        ) as result:
            if result.error:
                raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=result.error_msg)
            user = await result.fetch_one()
            if not user:
                raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="用户不存在")
            return user

    return await service.get_user(user_id)

    add_parser.add_argument("email", help="邮箱")

    args = parser.parse_args()

    # Create engine
    engine = Engine(
        host=args.host,
        port=args.port,
        user=args.user,
        password=args.password
    )

    await engine.connect()

    # Select database
    async with engine.execute(f"USE {args.database}"):
        pass

    # Create CLI instance
    cli = UserCLI(engine)

    # Execute command
    if args.command == "list":
        await cli.list_users()
    elif args.command == "add":
        await cli.add_user(args.name, args.email)

    await engine.disconnect()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

These examples cover the main usage scenarios of asmysql v2 version and can be modified and extended according to actual needs.

docs.title: Q: How to check connection pool status?
docs.text:
A: Use the engine.status attribute:

status = engine.status
print(status)

docs.title: Q: What's the difference between streaming query and regular query?
docs.text: A: - Regular Query: Loads all results into memory, suitable for small datasets - Streaming Query: Returns results row by row, does not consume memory, suitable for large datasets

docs.title: Q: How to customize result type?
docs.text:
A: Use the result_class parameter, supports tuple, dict, or custom model classes:

async with engine.execute(
    "SELECT * FROM users",
    result_class=dict,  # or custom model class
) as result:
    users = await result.fetch_all()

docs.title: Q: How to handle transactions?
docs.text:
A: Since v2.3.0, a "server-side auto-commit + transaction-state fallback" mechanism is used: the pool is fixed at autocommit=True; successful statements with an open transaction are committed, failed statements are rolled back automatically:

engine = Engine(url="...")
await engine.connect()

# Write operations are auto-committed by the server, persisted on success
# Failed statements are ROLLBACKed automatically, errors written to result.error

docs.title: Q: Are write statements with stream=True committed?
docs.text: A: Yes. v2.3.0 fixes the silent data loss caused by uncommitted streaming writes in older versions: stream=True + writes without result sets are committed immediately after execution according to the transaction state; streaming statements with result sets (such as CALL returning result sets) defer the commit until the cursor closes.

docs.title: Q: Are cross-statement transactions supported?
docs.text: A: No. Each execute() in v2 commits independently; a manual BEGIN / START TRANSACTION is committed immediately after execution. For transaction boundaries, combine operations into a single statement or a stored procedure.

docs.title: Q: When a task is cancelled (wait_for timeout / TaskGroup), is the statement rolled back?
docs.text: A: Not necessarily. Cancellation only interrupts the client-side wait, not SQL already sent: under autocommit=1, writes already completed by the server are independent transactions and are already committed — cancellation ≠ rollback. On cancellation the connection is discarded synchronously and the slot reclaimed; CancelledError propagates (it does not enter result.error); a cancelled Result is abandoned entirely — do not read its attributes or retry it. Cancellation while queued in acquire means the statement definitely did not execute and can be safely retried.

docs.title: Q: What if disconnect() keeps waiting and never returns?
docs.text: A: By default disconnect_timeout=None waits forever for all connections to return. Since v2.6.0, abandoned (garbage-collected) unclosed Result objects no longer cause an infinite wait — their connections are synchronously discarded with pool bookkeeping completed (emitting a ResourceWarning); only Result objects that are still referenced and unclosed keep it waiting. Make sure every Result is closed via async with / async for / close(); when convergence guarantees are needed, configure a finite timeout explicitly (e.g. disconnect_timeout=30): on timeout all in-use connections are terminated automatically with a ResourceWarning, and in-flight queries receive error_no=2013. Externally cancelling disconnect also terminates and converges.

docs.title: Q: How to clean up an Engine in synchronous shutdown scenarios (atexit / no event loop)?
docs.text: A: Use engine.terminate() (since v2.5.0): synchronous forced cleanup that does not wait for connections to return, immediately closes all in-use connections and severs in-flight queries, and cleans up idle connections best-effort; it is idempotent and safe to register via atexit.register(engine.terminate). You can connect() again afterwards to reuse the Engine. The Engine also ships a __del__ safety net: if it is GC'd without being disconnected, it emits a ResourceWarning and terminates automatically — but production code should still clean up explicitly (await engine.disconnect() inside an event loop, terminate() in synchronous hooks). See Connection Management.

docs.title: Q: How to get error information?
docs.text:
A: Through result.error, result.error_no, and result.error_msg attributes:

async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM invalid_table") as result:
    if result.error:
        print(f"Error code: {result.error_no}")
        print(f"Error message: {result.error_msg}")

docs.title: Q: Why does result.error have no traceback?
docs.text: A: Since v2.4.0, the __traceback__ frame chain is deliberately severed (set to None) when the error is stored, breaking the "Result → exception → frame → Result" reference cycle — otherwise holding result.error long-term (e.g. in an error audit list) would also retain the whole Result and the frame's local variables. Use error_no / error_msg and the SQL in result.query for troubleshooting; re-raising the exception produces a fresh traceback at the raise site.

docs.title: Q: How to batch insert data?
docs.text:
A: Use the execute_many() method:

data = [("张三", "zhangsan@example.com"), ("李四", "lisi@example.com")]
async with engine.execute_many("INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (%s, %s)", data) as result:
    print(f"Inserted {result.row_count} records")

docs.title: Q: How to share Engine instance across different modules?
docs.text:
A: You can create an Engine instance at application startup, then share it through dependency injection or global variables:

# app.py
engine = Engine(url="mysql://...")
await engine.connect()

# service.py
from app import engine


class UserService(AsMysql):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(engine)

docs.title: Q: Can an Engine be reused across multiple asyncio.run() calls / event loops?
docs.text: A: Yes, but you must "disconnect in the original loop → connect in the new loop" (since v2.4.0 the internal lock is rebuilt when the loop changes). An aiomysql pool is bound to its loop at creation and a live pool cannot be shared across loops: connecting/executing in a new loop without disconnecting first raises a ConnectionError with a clear message. See the "Reuse Across Event Loops" section in Connection Management.

docs.title: Q: How to set connection pool size?
docs.text:
A: Set based on application concurrency and database server performance:

  • Low concurrency applications: min_pool_size=2, max_pool_size=10
  • Medium concurrency: min_pool_size=5, max_pool_size=50
  • High concurrency applications: min_pool_size=10, max_pool_size=100+

docs.title: Q: How to handle connection timeout?
docs.text:
A: You can set connection timeout through the connect_timeout parameter:

engine = Engine(
    url="mysql://...",
    connect_timeout=10,  # 10 seconds timeout
)

docs.title: Q: Are AsMysql instances garbage collected automatically? Do I need to call release manually?
docs.text:
A: No, they are not unregistered automatically. The instance table holds strong references keyed by (subclass, engine object), so __del__ never triggers and garbage collection does not clean up entries.

  • Web services call UserService.release(engine) during lifespan shutdown; CLI calls it at the end of each round (or release() to clear the whole table)
  • Stale entries whose engine is disconnected (is_connected is False) are lazily removed on the next construction miss
  • release() only releases the table's strong references; it does not close the connection pool, which remains the responsibility of engine.disconnect()

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: This guide will help you get started with asmysql v2 quickly.

docs.title: Method 1: Using Engine Class
docs.text:
The Engine class is an independent MySQL connection engine that can be used directly:

import asyncio
from asmysql import Engine

# Create MySQL connection engine
engine = Engine(url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/?charset=utf8mb4")

async def main():
    # Connect to MySQL
    await engine.connect()

    # Execute SQL statement
    async with engine.execute("SELECT user, host FROM mysql.user") as result:
        async for item in result.iterate():
            print(item)

    # Disconnect from MySQL
    await engine.disconnect()

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Method 2: Using AsMysql Class
docs.text:
The AsMysql class is used for business logic development, ready to use by inheritance:

import asyncio
from asmysql import Engine, AsMysql

# Create MySQL connection engine
engine = Engine(url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/?charset=utf8mb4")

# Write business logic class
class UserService(AsMysql):
    async def get_all_users(self):
        async with self.client.execute("SELECT user, host FROM mysql.user") as result:
            if result.error:
                print(f"Error code: {result.error_no}, Error message: {result.error_msg}")
            else:
                async for item in result.iterate():
                    print(item)

async def main():
    # Connect to MySQL
    await engine.connect()

    # Create business logic instance
    user_service = UserService(engine)

    # Execute business logic
    await user_service.get_all_users()

    # Disconnect from MySQL
    await engine.disconnect()

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Standard Usage (Unified Forms)
docs.text:
Since v2.6.0, SQL execution recommends only the following unified safe forms, all of which close/release connections automatically:

  • async with engine.execute(...) as result: — context manager, closes automatically on exit (including exception paths);
  • async for row in engine.execute(...): — direct iteration, closes automatically when iteration completes or on break;
  • fetch_all() / iterate() — close automatically after data is exhausted;
  • Statements without result sets (INSERT/UPDATE/DDL, etc.) — close the cursor and return the connection automatically after execution.
# Standard form 1: async with
async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s", (1,)) as result:
    user = await result.fetch_one()

# Standard form 2: async for (also releases safely on break)
async for row in engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users", stream=True):
    process(row)

❌ Not recommended: bare execution r = engine.execute(...); await r() followed by fetch_one() / fetch_many() without close(). Such usage can only rely on the GC safety net to discard the connection (see "Commit and Connection Release Semantics" below) and is not a standard form.

docs.title: fetch_one() - Get Single Record
docs.text:
async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s", (1,)) as result:
    user = await result.fetch_one()
    if user:
        print(user)

docs.title: fetch_many() - Get Multiple Records
docs.text:
async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users") as result:
    users = await result.fetch_many(10)  # Get 10 records
    for user in users:
        print(user)

docs.text:
async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users") as result:
    all_users = await result.fetch_all()
    print(f"Total {len(all_users)} records")

async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users") as result:
    async for user in result.iterate():

    print(user)

# Method 2: Using async with then iterate
async with engine.execute("SELECT * FROM users") as result:
    async for user in result:
        print(user)

docs.title: Error Attributes
docs.text:
• result.error: Error exception object (MySQLError or None)
  • result.error_no: Error code (integer, 0 when no error)
  • result.error_msg: Error message (string, empty string when no error)

Since v2.4.0, result.error is stored with its __traceback__ set to None (severing the reference cycle between the exception's stack frames and the Result to avoid memory retention). Use error_no / error_msg and the SQL in result.query for troubleshooting; holding result.error long-term no longer keeps the Result object alive; re-raising the exception produces a fresh traceback at the raise site.

docs.title: Commit and Connection Release Semantics
docs.text:
• Successful statements: COMMIT is issued automatically when the server reports an open transaction (under autocommit=True, regular statements are auto-committed by the server and the client does not commit twice);
  • Failed statements: ROLLBACK is issued automatically; partial writes are never committed; errors from the commit/rollback itself are also written to result.error;
  • Statements without result sets (INSERT/UPDATE/DDL, etc.): the cursor is closed and the connection returned automatically after execution;
  • Statements with result sets: the connection is returned when data is exhausted, on close(), or on async with exit; transactions of streaming statements with result sets are committed at that point;
  • Connections whose cursor close, commit/rollback, or init_sql failed are discarded and never reused from the pool;
  • Task cancellation (CancelledError): the connection is discarded synchronously and the slot returned; the cancellation signal propagates and does not enter result.error; a cancelled Result is abandoned entirely — do not read its attributes or retry it.
  • Since v2.5.0, after close() or the automatic release of statements without result sets, the result.pool reference is cleared (type Optional[Pool]): caching closed Result objects no longer pins the connection pool and the event loop;
  • Since v2.6.0, GC safety net: an executed Result that was not properly closed, when garbage-collected, synchronously discards its connection (closes the transport without sending COM_QUIT) and completes pool bookkeeping, emitting a ResourceWarning; the connection is not returned to the pool for reuse, uncommitted transactions are rolled back by the server, and already auto-committed data is unaffected; disconnect() no longer hangs forever because of this. The safety net is only a fallback for misuse — production code must use the standard forms above;
  • Executing an unexecuted Result after close() raises RuntimeError (Result is closed and cannot be executed again); re-entering async with on an already executed Result remains a no-op and never re-executes.

docs.title: Execution Statistics
docs.text:
async with engine.execute("INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (%s)", ("张三",)) as result:
    # Affected rows
    print(f"Affected rows: {result.row_count}")

    # Last inserted ID (only for INSERT statements)
    print(f"Last inserted ID: {result.last_rowid}")

Note: - row_count returns None when using streaming query (stream=True) - row_count returns None when an error occurs - last_rowid is only valid for INSERT statements

docs.title: Auto-Commit Mechanism
docs.text: Since v2.3.0, a "server-side auto-commit + transaction-state fallback" mechanism is used: the connection pool is fixed at autocommit=True (built-in library behavior, no configuration parameter), and normal statements are auto-committed by the server. The client no longer parses SQL text to distinguish reads from writes; it only issues a fallback commit when the server reports that a transaction is still open.

docs.title: Commit on Success
docs.text:
After a statement executes successfully, the client checks the server transaction state (the IN_TRANS flag):

  • No open transaction (regular reads/writes under autocommit=True): nothing is done, the server has already auto-committed;
  • An open transaction exists (e.g. init_sql set autocommit to 0): COMMIT is executed automatically.
# Write operations are auto-committed by the server, no manual control needed
async with engine.execute(
    "INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (%s)", ("张三",)
) as result:
    pass  # Persisted on success

This mechanism treats all statements equally: WITH ... UPDATE/DELETE, writes starting with comments, OPTIMIZE, DO, and other statements missed by the old keyword whitelist are now committed correctly.

docs.title: Rollback on Failure
docs.text:
When a statement fails, if the connection is in a transaction or autocommit is disabled, ROLLBACK is executed automatically; partial writes of a failed statement are never committed. Errors are still written to result.error without raising exceptions.

async with engine.execute("INSERT INTO users (id) VALUES (1)") as result:
    if result.error is not None:
        print(result.error_no, result.error_msg)  # Failure rolled back, just check the error

docs.title: Commit Timing in Stream Mode
docs.text:
• stream=True + no result set (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, etc.): committed immediately after execution according to the transaction state; writes are persisted normally;
  • stream=True + result set (SELECT, CALL returning result sets, etc.): an immediate COMMIT would break the streaming protocol, so the commit is deferred until the cursor is closed (close() / async with exit / data exhausted).
# Streaming reads: the transaction (if any) is committed when the cursor closes after reading
async with engine.execute(
    "SELECT * FROM large_table",
    stream=True
) as result:
    async for row in result:
        process(row)

docs.title: No Cross-Statement Transactions
docs.text: v2 does not support multi-statement transactions across execute() calls: a manual BEGIN / START TRANSACTION is committed immediately after that statement executes. For business logic requiring transaction boundaries, combine operations into a single statement or a stored procedure.

docs.title: Connection Pool Configuration
docs.text:
The connection pool is created with autocommit=True as built-in library behavior:

  • Each connection defaults to auto-commit, consistent with the MySQL server default;
  • The client only issues a fallback COMMIT when the server reports an open transaction, and ROLLBACK on failure;
  • No autocommit configuration parameter is provided; if a backend rejects the SET AUTOCOMMIT handshake, the library internally falls back to the server default and emits a warning;
  • Non-transactional backends (such as ClickHouse) never set the transaction-state flag, so the client sends no redundant COMMIT.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text: v2.0.0 is a completely refactored version that is incompatible with v1. Main changes include:

docs.title: 1. Architecture Refactoring
docs.text:
• Separated Engine and AsMysql Classes
  • New Engine class: Independent MySQL connection engine, can be used standalone

  • Execution Method Changes

  • v1: AsMysql self.client.execute(...)
  • v2: AsMysql self.client.execute(...) (unchanged, but client is now an Engine instance)

  • error: Get complete error exception object

  • Streaming Query Support 

    result = await engine.execute("SELECT * FROM large_table", stream=True)
async for row in result:

docs.text:
• execute() Method
  • Support for stream parameter: Enable streaming query

  • Support for multiple calling methods:

    • result = await engine.execute(...)

docs.title: 4. Type Hints
docs.text:
• Complete type hint support

docs.title: 1. Connection Init SQL (init_sql)
docs.text:
Added init_sql parameter to automatically execute preset SQL on each new TCP connection's first use. Ideal for ClickHouse async insert configuration, MySQL session variable setup, and similar scenarios.

Background:

In databases like ClickHouse, SET statements are scoped at the TCP connection level. Previously, SET had to be manually executed before every INSERT to configure async insert parameters, which was redundant and inefficient. The init_sql feature moves this capability down to the engine layer for automatic per-connection initialization.

How It Works:

  • init_sql execution is implemented in Result.__call__()
  • Uses weakref.WeakKeyDictionary with Pool as key to track initialized connection IDs (id(conn))
  • Executes init_sql on first SQL execution of a new connection; skips on subsequent reuses
  • When a connection is recycled via pool_recycle, the new connection re-executes init_sql
  • After init_sql execution, commit() is called immediately to ensure SET statements take effect

Usage:

from asmysql import Engine

# Via keyword argument
engine = Engine(
    host="192.168.62.195",
    port=9004,
    user="default",
    password="",
    init_sql=(
        "SET async_insert = 1, wait_for_async_insert = 0, "
        "async_insert_busy_timeout_ms = 1000, "
        "max_execution_time = 30"
    ),
)
await engine.connect()

# Via URL parameter
engine = Engine(
    url="mysql://user:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/?init_sql=SET SESSION wait_timeout=600"
)
await engine.connect()

Backward Compatible:

init_sql defaults to None. When not provided, behavior is identical to v2.0.0 — no impact on existing code.

docs.title: 1. Auto-Commit Mechanism Refactored
docs.text:
Removed auto_commit Engine parameter and commit execute/Result parameter, replaced with SQL statement type-based auto-commit mechanism:

  • Result internally uses _should_commit() method to analyze the first keyword of SQL statements
  • Write operation keywords (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, REPLACE, CREATE, ALTER, DROP, etc.) automatically COMMIT after execution
  • Read operations (SELECT) do not trigger COMMIT
  • stream=True mode does not auto-COMMIT (to avoid interrupting the stream)

Migration Guide:

# v2.0.0 usage (deprecated)
engine = Engine(url="...", auto_commit=False)
result = await engine.execute("INSERT ...", commit=False)

# v2.1.0 usage
engine = Engine(url="...")
async with engine.execute("INSERT ...") as result:
    pass  # Write operations auto-commit

docs.title: Bug Fixes
docs.text:
• Fix fetch_all() connection leak for custom result types: When result_class is a custom class (e.g., Pydantic BaseModel), return _data exited before close(), leaking one connection per call. Unified return path to ensure close() always executes
  • Fix double connection release after query error: __call__() except branch closed cursor and released connection but didn't nullify __cursor. Added self.__cursor = None in except block
  • Fix async for + break connection leak: __aiter__ returned self, so after break, connection was never released. Rewritten as async generator with try/finally
  • Fix Result.__call__() only catching MySQLError causing connection leak: Non-MySQL exceptions were uncaught, leaving acquired connections unreleased. Changed to except Exception with re-raise for non-MySQL errors
  • Fix __del__ safety net crashes: __del__ during GC had no error handling and self.pool could be None. Added try/except and pool null check
  • Fix echo_sql_log URL parameter cannot be set to False: ?echo_sql_log=false was parsed as True. Now correctly parses boolean strings
  • Fix or operator overriding legitimate falsy values: Engine(min_pool_size=0) had 0 overridden to default. Unified to x if x is not None else default
  • Fix connect()/disconnect() concurrent race conditions: Multiple concurrent coroutines could create multiple pools or double-close. Added asyncio.Lock protection
  • Fix execute() passing self.__pool (possibly None): Disconnected calls produced Result with None pool. Now uses self.pool property
  • Fix Result[type[T]] generic parameter semantic error: Should be Result[T]. Corrected generic parameter
  • Fix release_connections() missing null check: Called before connect(), raised AttributeError. Added null check
  • Remove @lru_cache decorators: @lru_cache on __repr__/__str__ held strong references to self, preventing GC. Removed caching
  • Fix error_msg not using err_msg() formatting: Lost fallback handling for empty strings. Now calls err_msg() function
  • Fix iterate() truthiness check inconsistency: if data: treated empty tuples as falsy. Unified to is not None check
  • Fix row_count/last_rowid/row_number AttributeError after close: Accessing these properties after cursor was nullified caused crashes. Added null check
  • DDL/DML statements auto-release connection: When cursor.description is None (DDL/INSERT/UPDATE etc.), automatically closes cursor and releases connection back to pool, while caching rowcount / lastrowid

docs.title: 1. AsMysql Constructive Singleton
docs.text:
The AsMysql base class now provides a process-wide constructive singleton: instances are reused with (subclass, engine object) as the key, so business subclasses need no singleton code of their own.

Background:

In Web services (e.g., creating mysql_engine_master in lifespan) and CLI loops, business code repeatedly constructs the same business class. Previously each construction produced a new object, so state could not be shared within the process; now the base class manages instance reuse centrally, with zero iteration and zero temporary allocation on the hit path.

How it works:

  • AsMysql.__new__ maintains a process-wide instance table keyed by (subclass, engine object)
  • Same subclass + same engine object: the same instance is always reused; on a hit __init__ still runs, but only reassigns the same engine (idempotent)
  • Different engine objects / different subclasses: each keeps its own instance, isolated from each other
  • The instance table holds strong references to engines; on a miss, stale entries whose engine is disconnected (is_connected is False) are lazily removed to prevent unbounded cache growth

Usage:

from asmysql import Engine, AsMysql

engine = Engine(url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/")
await engine.connect()

class UserService(AsMysql):
    pass

assert UserService(engine) is UserService(engine)  # same instance

docs.title: 2. release() Unregisters Instances
docs.text:
Added the AsMysql.release() class method to explicitly unregister instance table entries (it only releases strong references, not disconnect):

# Remove this engine's entries across all subclasses, returns the removed count
removed = UserService.release(engine)

# Clear the whole table (Web service lifespan shutdown, end of each CLI round), returns the removed count
removed = UserService.release()
  • Releasing the same engine repeatedly returns 0 without raising KeyError
  • The connection pool is still closed by whoever owns the engine via engine.disconnect()

docs.title: Behavior Changes
docs.text: • Construction behavior of AsMysql(engine) changes: repeated construction with the same subclass + same engine object now returns the same instance. Business classes that rely on a fresh instance per construction (e.g., storing request-scoped state on instance attributes) should use local variables inside methods or reuse the instance explicitly

docs.title: 1. Auto-Commit Mechanism Rework: Server Autocommit + Transaction-State Fallback
docs.text:
• The pool changes from autocommit=False (hardcoded) to autocommit=True (built-in library behavior, no new configuration parameters); normal statements are auto-committed by the server.
  • The SQL first-keyword whitelist (_WRITE_KEYWORDS / _should_commit()) is removed; SQL text is no longer parsed to distinguish reads from writes. The server transaction state (the IN_TRANS flag) is the single source of truth.
  • Unified rule: successful statements with an open transaction are COMMITted, failed statements are ROLLBACKed (the failure check includes a supplementary check for disabled autocommit).
  • If a backend rejects the SET AUTOCOMMIT handshake, the library internally falls back to the server default (autocommit=None) and emits a RuntimeWarning, transparent to callers.

Behavior change comparison:

Scenario Before After stream=True + INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE Not committed, rolled back on connection return (silent data loss) Committed, persisted normally WITH ... UPDATE/DELETE, writes starting with # comments, OPTIMIZE/DO, etc. Missed by the whitelist, not committed Committed according to server transaction state Regular INSERT (non-stream) Client-side COMMIT Server auto-commit, no duplicate client COMMIT Connection return after SELECT Transaction residue, connection closed by aiomysql Returned after the transaction ends, connections truly reused Failed statements Possible transaction residue ROLLBACK, partial writes never committed Manual BEGIN / START TRANSACTION Unclear behavior Committed immediately after execution (v2 does not support cross-statement transactions)

docs.title: 2. Connection Handling on Commit/Rollback Failure
docs.text: Connections whose COMMIT/ROLLBACK, cursor close, or init_sql failed are always discarded (closed, then pool bookkeeping only) and never reused from the pool; errors are written to result.error without raising exceptions.

docs.title: 1. disconnect_timeout Configuration (Default None, Backward Compatible)
docs.text:
Engine adds disconnect_timeout: Optional[float] = None (class attribute default, constructor parameter, and URL query parameter all supported; none in URL means None):

  • None (default): waits forever for all connections to return, fully consistent with legacy behavior;
  • Finite value: after the graceful wait times out, emits a ResourceWarning and forcibly terminates all in-use connections, guaranteed to converge; in-flight queries receive error_no=2013;
  • <= 0: no wait, terminate immediately;
  • If disconnect itself is cancelled, it also terminates and re-raises; the cancellation path always converges.

docs.title: 2. Explicit Warning for execute_many([])
docs.text: An empty parameter list no longer silently executes nothing: no connection is acquired, no SQL is sent, a UserWarning is emitted, row_count=0, last_rowid=None.

docs.title: Bug Fixes
docs.text:
• Silent loss of streaming writes: write statements with stream=True are now committed correctly (immediately without result sets, deferred to cursor close with result sets).
  • Keyword whitelist misses: WITH, comment-prefixed, OPTIMIZE/ANALYZE/DO, etc. are no longer missed.
  • Swallowed COMMIT failures: commit failures are written to result.error and the connection discarded, never returned with an open transaction.
  • GC address reuse in id(conn)-based init_sql tracking: replaced with a WeakSet tracking connections by object identity; new connections always re-execute init_sql.
  • Session loss from silent ping() reconnects: ping() removed from close() and execution paths (transaction end is what actually releases locks; ping cannot do this and rebuilds TCP).
  • Protocol pollution from closing unread streaming cursors: cursor close failure discards the connection; no COMMIT is attempted.
  • Half-initialized connections returned after init_sql failure: discarded on failure; init_sql now runs on an independent buffered cursor, avoiding Commands out of sync on streaming cursors.
  • Connection leaks on CancelledError: on cancellation the connection is discarded synchronously and the slot reclaimed; CancelledError is re-raised (it does not enter result.error); cancellation while queued in acquire is safely retryable, a Result cancelled after acquire is abandoned entirely. __anext__ no longer swallows cancellation into StopAsyncIteration.
  • No retry after non-MySQLError: the unconditional finally setting of __executed is removed; non-MySQLError exceptions during acquire no longer block retrying the same Result.
  • disconnect() infinite wait: optional finite-timeout terminate fallback added (see New Features 1); default behavior unchanged.

docs.title: Semantic Boundaries (Please Note)
docs.text:
• Cancellation ≠ rollback: cancellation only interrupts the client-side wait; under autocommit=1, writes already completed by the server are committed and persisted.
  • No cross-statement transactions: each execute() commits independently.
  • Non-transactional backends such as ClickHouse never set the transaction-state flag: zero COMMIT on success paths; failure paths send one harmless ROLLBACK that is accepted (verified on 26.5.1).
  • BOM-prefixed statements are rejected by the MySQL 8 server (1064) — a visible error, not silent loss; leading WITH ... INSERT is invalid syntax in MySQL 8 (CTE INSERT must be trailing).

docs.text: Theme: memory retention and event loop binding fixes (risks 4/6 from the memory analysis report). No new public API; result.error semantics and Engine cross-loop behavior change. Analysis report: asmysql_v2_final_memory_analysis.md at the repository root.

docs.title: 1. result.error.__traceback__ is now None
docs.text:
When an error is stored (execution failure, COMMIT/ROLLBACK failure), the exception's __traceback__ is uniformly set to None, severing the "Result → exception → traceback frame → Result" reference cycle:

  • Before: holding result.error long-term (e.g. an error audit list) also retained the whole Result and the frame's local variables (conn/values, etc.), and __del__ never fired; even with no holder, the Result had to wait for a cyclic GC pass to be reclaimed.
  • After: the Result's reference count can reach zero immediately; holding the error no longer keeps the Result alive.
  • Unaffected: error_no, error_msg, result.query; the D4 "first error wins" semantics (a ROLLBACK failure does not overwrite the original error).
  • Trade-off: the original call stack is lost; re-raising the exception produces a fresh traceback at the raise site. Use error_no / error_msg and the SQL for troubleshooting.

docs.title: 2. Clear error for live pools across event loops
docs.text:
An aiomysql pool is bound to its event loop at creation time. With the pool still connected, calling connect(), accessing engine.pool, or calling execute() in a new event loop now raises:

ConnectionError: Engine 的连接池属于另一个事件循环，请先在原循环 disconnect()，或为新循环创建新 Engine

Previously this scenario either silently reused the wrong-loop pool (then failed in obscure ways) or raised asyncio's cryptic RuntimeError. Synchronous access without a running event loop keeps the legacy behavior.

docs.title: Engine reuse across event loops
docs.text:
The internal connect lock (_connect_lock) is automatically rebuilt when the event loop changes, supporting the "disconnect in the original loop → connect in the new loop" reuse pattern:

engine = Engine(url="mysql://root:pass@127.0.0.1:3306/")


async def job():
    await engine.connect()
    async with engine.execute("SELECT 1") as result:
        print(await result.fetch_one())
    await engine.disconnect()


asyncio.run(job())  # Event loop 1
asyncio.run(job())  # Event loop 2: the lock is rebuilt and the pool is recreated

Before the fix, once the lock experienced contention it bound to that loop, and a second asyncio.run() raised RuntimeError: ... is bound to a different event loop (Python 3.12's Lock contended path validates the loop while the uncontended fast path does not, so the failure was intermittent).

Semantic boundaries:

  • Sharing a live pool across loops is still unsupported (an aiomysql hard constraint); disconnect first;
  • An abandoned Engine whose loop has closed without disconnecting is not guaranteed to be cleanable in a new loop;
  • Concurrent connect() calls within the same loop are still serialized by the lock; behavior is unchanged.

docs.text:
• Risk 4 (Result ↔ traceback reference cycle): the three error storage sites (__call__ / __commit / __rollback) converge into __store_error, which severs the frame chain on storage.
  • Risk 6 (_connect_lock bound to the event loop): loop-aware lock rebuilding + a live-pool cross-loop guard (connect() and the pool property).
